name: infra_click_config
title: A click console script over a dataclass config overlaid from TOML, with two defects that are dataclass field defaults
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-infra: config resolution through the object every real project passes around
note: Two planted defects, both of which are values of dataclass FIELD DEFAULTS reached as `cfg.<field>` inside a helper that takes the config as a parameter - which is how every dataclass-configured project is written. MLV110 fires but only at 0.510, below the 0.60 Problems-panel threshold, with a correctly hedged message and an honest `config_unresolved` diagnostic. MLV112 does not fire at all and nothing declares its silence. Measured A/B: move the dataclass instance into the same scope as the DataLoader and both rules recover - MLV110 0.680 and MLV112 0.784 - so the whole loss is the one parameter hop, and `--dataflow ip` does not recover it either. See the domain-infra round-2 report, finding INFRA-R2-16. There is also no `if __name__ == "__main__":` anywhere in the package, by design: pyproject.toml declares `mlpkg = "mlpkg.cli:cli"` and that is the only entrypoint, which is exactly the situation MLV112 exists for.
stagesObserved: config, data, model, objective, train, eval and deliver present; preprocess absent, which is correct. `--relevance ml` and `--relevance all` are identical (4 files either way).

expected.defect: the training loader takes shuffle=cfg.shuffle, and TrainConfig.shuffle defaults to False (config.py line 35)
expected.why: the default `mlpkg train` run - no CLI flag, and config.toml sets no shuffle key - trains on 7200 rows in file order for all 30 epochs; observed at confidence 0.510, BELOW the 0.60 Problems-panel threshold, so a user running the VS Code extension never sees it

expected.defect: num_workers=cfg.num_workers with TrainConfig.num_workers defaulting to 8 (config.py line 36), in a package whose only entrypoint is a console script with no `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard
expected.why: macOS and Windows spawn worker processes that re-import the module; with no guard the import re-enters click's command group and the run either hangs or forks recursively. Not recovered: the dataclass default is not resolved through the `cfg` parameter, and no diagnostic declares the gap

forbidden.why: the validation loader passes the literal shuffle=False at line 66
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is at line 112, before the forward at 113
optimizer.step() is called at line 116, after loss.backward() at line 115
the order is zero_grad (112) -> forward (113) -> loss (114) -> backward (115) -> step (116)
the epoch loss is accumulated as running += loss.item(), a Python float
CosineAnnealingLR is epoch-cadence and scheduler.step() is called at line 118, in the epoch loop
evaluate() calls model.eval() at line 78 and model.train() at line 87 on the way out; the export command calls model.eval() at cli.py line 72
the export command calls model.eval() at line 72 before tracing, and traces one zero tensor rather than running a loop
evaluate() carries the @torch.no_grad() decorator at line 75
the accuracy comparison at line 84 is on model(features).argmax(dim=1), not on raw logits
TabularNet.forward returns self.head(self.body(x)) - raw logits - and nn.CrossEntropyLoss is fed exactly that
the model is moved at lines 96 and 132 and the eval loop moves every batch value at 82-83; the training loop moves them at 110-111
the device is chosen behind torch.cuda.is_available() at lines 93 and 130
seed_everything(cfg.seed) at line 92 calls random.seed, numpy.random.seed, torch.manual_seed and torch.cuda.manual_seed_all, and the synthetic draw uses np.random.default_rng(cfg.seed)
there is no sklearn splitter and no random_split; the cut is a literal fraction of a seeded draw
TabularNet.__init__ calls super().__init__() as its first statement at line 25
the body is an nn.Sequential; there is no plain list or dict of submodules
torch.save stores model.state_dict() at line 125 and torch.load passes weights_only=True at line 133
